title: Quinones's advice: play from the heart
summary: Quinones told him it is not what you do but how you do it.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: You see? And they're one of our greatest fans. They'll tell you that. Yeah. As far as a dance band, they'll tell you that. Yeah. That's why I'm saying, when you play music you've got to play it with feelings. It's a different profession from anything else. If you play music and it's blah, nothing comes out. You've got to play it from under your heart. Like the old man used to tell me that Francisco Quignones one day he was playing a solo on a guitar and I told him, I says, pro, I says, my God, I says, I really would be proud if I play just as half as good as what you do. He turns around to me and he tells me, he says, listen, Chinito, that was in Spanish because he couldn't speak English. He says, remember these words, what I'm going to tell you. He says, I'm an old man. He says, and you're nothing but a child. He says, but remember this because as long as you live, you're going to remember it. And believe me, he did. He says, it's not what you do, it's how you do it. He says, and never forget this. He says that everything you do, make it come from under here. He says, and you'll never go wrong. And believe me, up until this day, I'll remember that. And he was right. Yeah.
